question: Regulations (EC) No 1831/2003 and (EC) No 429/2008 govern authorisations for placing on the market and using feed additives in the European Union, as well as the compilation of technical dossiers and safety and efficacy criteria. Additives must be authorised and are subject to an evaluation of their safety and efficacy by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA).

The EFSA publishes regularly revised guidelines to help applicants in the compilation of dossiers. However, these guidelines include requirements that go beyond legislation and fail to observe the principle of proportionality. Moreover, failure to comply with EFSA requirements results in inconclusive advice, which forces petitioners to regularly redo studies on animals.

Fewer such studies should be conducted for animal welfare reasons. The imbalance between the regulatory framework and EFSA requirements creates uncertainty for applicants and operators in the sector, and stifles innovation, which has repercussions for EU competitiveness. 1.
What is the Commission's involvement in EFSA's work on feed additives?
What role does the Commission intend to play in the establishment of an assessment framework by EFSA?
How will the Commission strive to help European stakeholders to remain competitive on the animal feed market?
answer: In accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 (1) and Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 (2), the Commission’s role in the authorisation process of feed additives does not interfere with the European Food Safety Authority’s (EFSA) task to provide independent scientific opinions.

As a risk manager, the Commission’s tasks include mandating EFSA for scientific opinions and adopting risk management measures based on those opinions, taking into account Union law and other relevant legitimate factors. Additionally, the Commission sets detailed rules for applications presented for authorisation laid down in Regulation (EC) No 429/2008 (3).

According to Article 7(6) of Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003, EFSA is responsible for providing detailed guidance to assist applicants, which allows to consider the most recent scientific developments in the additives’ assessment, but this does not substitute for the obligation for applicants to comply with the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 and its implementing rules.

The Commission is handling swiftly many requests for additives’ authorisations to ensure market access for companies. It is also making full use of the existing legal framework to encourage innovation in the sector.

Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 September 2003 on additives for use in animal nutrition (Official Journal L 268, 18.10.2003, p. 29, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2003/1831/2021-03-27).

Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 January 2002 laying down the general principles and requirements of food law, establishing the European Food Safety Authority and laying down procedures in matters of food safety (Official Journal L 31, 1.2.2002, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2002/178/2022-07-01).

Commission Regulation (EC) No 429/2008 of 25 April 2008 on detailed rules for the implementation of Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the preparation and the presentation of applications and the assessment and the authorisation of feed additives (Official Journal L 133, 22.5.2008, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2008/429/2021-03-27).
